You should be aware of fact that we have received testimony from people who were present in that school. So what we want to know is how you perceived these problems. If you can answer the question, answer it. If you can't, just say so, and we'll move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to remind you, Mr. President, that there was a conflict because people weren't free to move Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond around. There were various incidents. People were killed. I said that I was imprisoned, that half of the command was imprisoned. We didn't take any measures in relation to these incidents because we did not want an armed conflict to break out because we had an enemy who was too strong on one side, on Vlasic, on Mount Vlasic, and we had a conflict with the Croats, with the HVO. And it wasn't to our advantage. We were endangered. Our lives were at risk. I wouldn't want to answer your question by saying I don't know. But I have also said that before the 8th of June, the HVO attacked the village of Ricice and expelled the population from that village. And then the village of Velika Bukovica was attacked, and 87 civilians were taken from that village to Busovaca. In the course of the fighting and over a two-day period, seven members of our brigade were killed. These people were taken away, and we waited to see what would happen to these people. And I have mentioned two reasons for which the people were kept in the school: first of all, we wanted to exchange them for people taken away by HVO members; and the second reason was we wanted to ensure that they were secure. Believe me, if we had said they could go home, they would have refused to go home for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Officially, my time would have been expired now, but since the last 10 minutes or so, 15 minutes maybe, I couldn't ask any question myself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much more time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would need 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well naturally, we'll give just as much time to Defence counsel. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have, after this last conversation, just one question left to this topic. Mr. Jusic, are you aware that there is an article in the Third Geneva Convention, Article 17, which provides - I will read it to you in the French language, and it will be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, Article 17 of the Third Geneva Convention is applied to an international armed conflict. And that is not part of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you're well aware that there is a dispute as to the nature of the armed conflict. In your submissions, you mentioned an armed conflict. The Defence would like to know whether the Prosecution is claiming that there was the existence of an international armed conflict or an internal armed conflict. Given that Article 17 of the Third Convention relates to international armed conflicts, the Defence claims that this represents a problem. Before you address this issue, you should first ask the witness whether he is aware of the Geneva Conventions and develop the subject on that basis. Try to rephrase the question without addressing the issue of the international or internal nature of the conflict. You can deal with legal issues since we have a lawyer as a witness. So you could approach the question from a legal point of view. Please go ahead. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, I will very soon move on to another topic. Just, are you aware of the existence of the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. As a lawyer, I couldn't say that I'm not aware of the Geneva Conventions. I told you that I studied international law, and I passed the exam and obtained my degree. So I'm aware of these conventions. I knew there was an international court. I knew there was an international court in The Hague. I was aware of all of these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the Third Geneva Convention, do you know what the topic of the Third Geneva Convention is?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't need to study that for my exams. What I studied 25 or 30 years ago, well, as far as I can remember, I studied what I needed to perform my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you were questioning people, were you questioning alone, or you had some colleagues with you?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I was alone with them. The person who would bring them to the office would stand outside the door. When I finished with one person, that person would leave, another person would be brought in. That's how we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you first tell me, were there other people doing the interrogations, or were you the only person doing the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Perhaps before I arrived, someone else interrogated them. But I don't know. While I was there, while I interrogated the people there, my superior said that two young men had arrived from Zenica, either from the corps -- perhaps they were from the corps. And he said that they would take statements from some individuals. I was told to allow them to do so, and I allowed them to take statements. They were there for a day or two, no longer. They took statements from some individuals and then left, after which I continued to do my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you were present when these two persons from Zenica were asking questions, or you were outside the room?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I could have been there with them, but I could also have left. So I listened to them questioning a few individuals, but I would also leave the premises. I wasn't present at all times during their interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And were these people from the military police in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: They didn't introduce themselves to me. But my superior told me this is what they were going to do, and if he told me that I should allow them to do this without checking their identity, et cetera, well, naturally this is something that I accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was your superior who told you to permit these two military police officers to ask questions? What's the name?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this question is entirely inappropriate. The witness said that he didn't know who they were, and he said that he thought that they came from Zenica. My learned colleague said, Who was the superior who allowed those two military police officers to interrogate individuals? So this question is entirely inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now that I look at the transcript, it seems that there were two persons who arrived there. So you should proceed as follows -- well, in fact, I'll ask the witness the question. Otherwise we'll waste a lot of time. You said at a given point in time - we don't know when - two persons arrived from Zenica. Were these two individuals men or women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two young men, as I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So these men, were they wearing civilian clothes or were they in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in uniform, in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So they were wearing military uniforms. Did they have insignia or badges of any kind? Which unit did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They probably had insignia of some kind, but I can't remember what sort of insignia they had on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So were these members of the HVO? Were these men members of the HVO? I can see that you are smiling. So they could only be members of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, they couldn't have been HVO members. But as I have already said, perhaps the Chamber didn't understand me, I said they were from Zenica. I said they were from the 3rd Corps. And I said that someone from Zenica sent them to us, a superior from Zenica sent them to us. That's what I said. Because I doubt that my superior would have allowed just anyone to go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But the 3rd Corps had up to 32.000 troops. That's what we have been told. As this corps was divided into various sorts of units, did these men belong to one of the units, the 7th Brigade, the 312th, the 306th Brigade, et cetera, et cetera? Or were these men men who only reported to the main staff of the -- to the headquarters of the 3rd Corps? Which unit did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't say the 3rd Corps had 32.000 members, because I don't know how many members the 3rd Corps had. I said that two young men arrived. My superior told me that they would be taking statements from some of the individuals who were present in the school. I was told to allow them to do so. As to whether they were from the 3rd Corps command or from the 3rd Corps military police battalion or from the KP Dom or from the supreme command, I really don't know. I assume they had some sort of insignia, but I can't remember the insignia that they had on them. And believe me, I cannot really say which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you can't tell us which unit they belonged to. On the basis of the questions that they put, since you were present there, were -- would you say that these men were lawyers, judges, prosecutors, plumbers, drivers? Who were they? What would you say on the basis of the questions you heard them put?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, I didn't know what they were by profession, nor do I know that now. But I assume that they had been sent there by our superiors. I was present when they interrogated these men. I wanted to see whether they were better at it. I wanted to see whether I could learn something from them. I was present on a couple of occasions, and I saw that they were no better at interrogating these people than I was. And as to what their profession was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you're telling us that you were present to see whether they were better prepared to interrogate these people than you were, and you decided they weren't. But if you are an excellent interrogator, perhaps they are interrogated, too [as interpreted]. But let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On page 48, line 18, you mentioned these two persons were from the corps. You were referring to the 3rd Corps, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness said he came from superior command. I don't know whether it was the 3rd Corps, the battalion, the supreme command. This was in response to your question. Why is the Prosecution asking the witness the same question since this question has been answered by the witness on two occasions already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he said that they came from the 3rd Corps, but he doesn't know from which unit. So please move on, otherwise we'll end up wasting more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You testified earlier that there were many neighbours of you in the school. So you knew some of them. Were you aware that there was also a survivor of the Maline-Bikose incident in your school?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm surprised to see that you are addressing this matter since it's not something that has been discussed yet. It's not something that has been raised by the Defence either. Why are you trying to ask the witness this question? Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has answered my learned colleague's question a number of times. He said that he found out about the events in Bikose only a little later. So how could he know whether anyone had survived that event if he wasn't familiar with the event at all? So the questions being put to this witness now are now inappropriate. They are being put to him to make the witness say something he never wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness initially said that in Miletici and Maline -- as far as Miletici and Maline are concerned, he knew nothing when he was performing his duties. It was only one month later that he obtained certain information. And now you are asking him -- you are saying that there was a survivor from Maline, and you can see why there is a problem. I'll try to deal with this contradiction. Among the civilians accommodated in the Mehurici school, among those you saw, were there any who spoke about events that they had personally experienced? Did you hear anything about such events? As far as you know, among the people who were there, did anyone tell you about an event of any significance? Can you remember any such cases? Or were you under the impression that these were good citizens who hadn't experienced anything in particular apart from the fact that they were being kept in the school for the purpose of their own safety? What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, I've already said none of the people who were there from whom I took statements told me anything. I only knew what I've already testified about. And I only learned about these events later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Zeljko Puselja?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Zeljko Puselja. We lived in the same neighbourhood. He is a good guy. I knew him very well, I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Zeljko Puselja in the Mehurici school in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him in the school. He was there. I know that his arm was bandaged. He had been given first aid, apparently. I don't know who from. I took a statement from him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were you the only person who took a statement of Zeljko Puselja or were there others in the room when you were doing it, or taking a statement afterwards from him?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I don't know whether I was with them when Zeljko was being interviewed or not. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know the date when you interviewed him approximately? Directly after you were arriving, a few days after you were arriving?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: It took a few days for me to take all the statements. And during that period of time, I took a statement from him as well. I arrived in Mehurici on the 8th of June. I was taking statements over a period of a few days. And during that period, at some point in time, I took a statement from him as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In what condition was Mr. Puselja when he talked to you? You mentioned already he had a bandage around his arm. But what was his general condition?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: At the moment when I spoke to him, his general condition was good. His life was not threatened. His arm was bandaged up to his elbow. But his general condition was good.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since he was your neighbour, you knew that -- You took a statement from him. Do you recall any particulars of what he told you? First of all, let me rephrase. Why did you take a statement of -- why did you take a statement of him?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The principle was the same. He fell into the right age group. He was somewhere between 20 and 60. And that was the main reason. There was no other reason at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you recall any particulars of what Mr. Zeljko Puselja told you during the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't recall any details. This was about 13 years ago. I can't recall any of the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you never spoke again with him afterwards about your statement, since you told me you knew him? You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: After that, I didn't talk to him. People are currently returning to their homes. I could have bumped into him. I didn't. I would like to see him. I have never heard him say anything bad about me, about the way I treated him. Nobody for that matter said anything bad about me. And as to your question whether I ever met him after that, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sir, one of the witnesses who has appeared in front of this Trial Chamber testified that Mr. Zeljko Puselja had a fractured arm. Did you notice this at the time?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I believe that I've already answered that. At the moment when I spoke to him, his arm was bandaged up to the elbow. I don't know whether this was just a gauze bandage or a plaster. I don't know. In any case, his arm was bandaged. It may have been fractured for all I know. I can't tell you. I may have even asked him that, but I don't remember whether I did or not and what his answer was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember the statement you took from him or -- generally, the statements, where were you passing them on? You were forwarding them somewhere, I assume. To your superior, or were they going to somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I personally did not forward these statements, save to the person who actually ordered me to perform this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you are probably not aware where this person was forwarding the statement to; you just know you forwarded it to your superior who gave you the task, and then you don't know where they went to.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were forwarded at all. I was deployed to a different position. I went to work there. What happened to the statements, whether anybody forwarded them, used them, did anything with them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the persons coming from Zenica, you also -- did they also take statements with them, or you kept all the statements?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: They took their papers with them. They didn't give anything to me. In my view, they were my superiors, and it was my obligation to allow them to do their job as they best saw fit. As they were leaving, they said "We are not coming back. You just proceed and do what you're doing."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Does this imply that you could look at the content of the statements they took, or since they treated you as a kind of subordinate, you weren't even allowed to look into their statements?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I did not feel the need to read these statements. I was present during one or two interviews just to see what they were doing and compare their way of work with the way I do things. In my opinion, there was no need to ask them anything or to say anything to them. They just did their job, and then they left. Where they went to, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have some 10 minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusic, tell me, please, when you were interrogating the individuals who were accommodated in the buildings in Mehurici, did you ever use force? Did you ever threaten these people?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Never. I never used force or threat. I found myself in a very awkward situation to have to take statements from my former neighbours with whom I had very good neighbourly relations. We used to work in the same companies. In other words, I never used force. I even didn't wear a military uniform to avoid any discomfort. So when I took statements, I wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, you asked these persons questions. When they answered those questions, did they do it of their own free will without any coercion on your part?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I appreciated the situation that these people were in. They could not have felt at ease. However, my impression was, and I did my best to create such an atmosphere for them to tell me freely what they wanted to tell me. Some of them even told me that they were members of the HVO, who their commander was. Some even said that they could go to their villages and show us where the arms were, where the explosives were, where the minefields were. And I've already said that in cooperation with them, we did go to the villages and found those explosives and arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Exhibit P204. I don't know whether the witness still has it, or does he have to be provided with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have already read this document. I would like to draw your attention to the part that precedes the words "hereby order." In the introduction, is it said that it was the civilians who were involved in plunder as well as some individuals from the army? Is that what this document actually states?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: My opinion with regard to the facts that are mentioned in this document is relative to the prevention of plunder and arson committed by civilians. The document was drafted on the 18th of June which was immediately after the combat operations. I am not even sure that the combat operations were finished at the time. In any case, the front line was still open. And at that moment the brigade had two front lines, one of them on Mount Vlasic and the other one facing the HVO. It took a huge number of people to man those two lines. In the light of the fact that during the combat operations, some people got killed, a lot got wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that you have answered my question. My learned friend drew your attention to the date when this document was drafted, which is the 18th of June. And as far as I remember, you replied that measures were taken even before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown a series of documents, DH161/9, DH161/10, DH161/11, DH161/12, DH161/13, DH161/16, and DH162/2. Since I have these documents with me, I can assist the usher and ask to present these documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects because this issue of measures has been raised by the Defence in her examination-in-chief already. And I didn't elaborate on a new topic. So there was already a chance given for the Defence to elaborate on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any re-examination and the right to reply to such question has to do with the answers provided to the question put on cross-examination. Now you are introducing new documents. Why? Can you please explain to us what their contents are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Document P204 was not used on cross-examination. It was the document that was shown to the witness by the Prosecution. As for the new series of documents, this arises from the Prosecutor's question relative to the date, the 18th of June 1993. He asked, Why didn't the army take any measures prior to this in order to prevent these incidents? I would like to show the witness all these documents and put just one question to him after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has put such a question to the witness. I remember that well. And the document in question was drafted on the 18th of June. And the question was how come that no prior measures were taken? And the witness responded there were other measures. Is that what you wanted to confirm with the witness? In that case, you can show the documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, can you please look at all of these documents and tell me what the dates on these documents are.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The 9th of June 1993, 10th of June 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The first document is 9th of June 1993. Who was it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: It was addressed to the units and staffs of the 3rd Corps. I believe that this K stands for the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the units and the staffs of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, the introductory part of this document, what does it convey?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: In order to prevent inappropriate behaviour of the members of the BH Army in the sense of combat activities against the HVO and to preserve the moral character of the BiH Army fighter, I hereby warrant --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the document dated the 9th of June. Can you please look at the second document. What's the date?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was this addressed to? Who was this document addressed to?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: To all subordinate units, and it was sent by the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the subject of this order? What does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The subject of this order are measures in place against plunder and destruction of property.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, the first document was DH161/9, and the second one is 161/10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document. What is the date on it?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: It is the 16th of June 1993, to the commands of all units, to the assistant commanders for security. And the subject is exchange of prisoners of war between the BiH Army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is DH161/11.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The following document bears the date 16 June 1993. It is a document marked urgent, and it -- it's regarding the delivery of order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: To the command of the operations group, to the commands of independent brigades, to all of them; to the commands of independent battalions, all of them; and to the municipal defence staff command. Actually, I don't understand the abbreviation. I believe it's the municipal staffs, to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Looking at the preamble of this order, can you tell us what does this order refer to? Can you please read this.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: On the basis of information received from the corps command and unverified details in connection with pillage and torching of citizens' property in the wake of combat operations, in order to establish the whole truth and in this connection to establish the whole truth -- this must be a printing error - I issue the following order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, this is the document 162/12.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The following document bears the date 16 June 1993. It was sent to the 306th Mountain Brigade, personally to the commander. And the subject is securing Guca Gora region.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is DH161/13.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The following document bears the date 19 June 1993, and it is addressed to all the subordinate units. It was sent by the command of the 3rd Corps. And the subject is prevention of arrest of civilians, pillage, and destruction of property.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is DH161/16.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, can you look at the last document.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: The date is 9th June 1993. It was sent to the Lasva Operations Group. And it regards your enactment and orders being issued following an enactment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it refers to the protection of civilians and their property?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, read it.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, assistance was requested in order to protect the property of civilians, and the corps was requested to provide assistance. And here, the corps command orders property to be protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is 162/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Having inspected these documents, having perused the contents thereof, Mr. Jusic, do these documents show you -- does it arise from these documents that the intention of the 3rd Corps was to prevent crimes, to carry out investigations, to punish the perpetrators thereof, and that these measures are being repeated in order for them to be accepted by the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: From these documents and from the facts that I am aware of, the 3rd Corps command invested a maximum effort, and they did as much as they could, like it says in one of the documents, in order to preserve the moral character of the BiH Army and its fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And my last question with this regard, Mr. Jusic, you have responded a number of questions and it was your intention to describe to us the very difficult situation in which the BiH Army units performed their task. The documents that I have just shown to you, do they show that in spite of these difficult conditions, measures were taken and BiH Army members were punished for every crime that they might have committed?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: According to what I know, in my brigade and in the corps, everything was done to prevent conflict. Once the conflict did happen, then everything was done that -- to make sure that international standards were respected and that people who were detained and people who were arrested would be protected, as well as their property that had remained abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Jusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's time for the break now. We'll resume at about 1.00, and we'll have 45 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have 45 minutes left for additional questions and the Judges' questions. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have a number of questions that concern the document shown by the Prosecution to the witness. Document P661 is the one concerned. I think the witness has it to his right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusic, you've already had the opportunity reading this document, and you have answered questions about it when these questions were put to you by the Prosecution. Kljaci is mentioned in the document, the village of Kljaci. I have a map here. But since you're from the area, could you just tell me what the distance between the village of Kljaci to the village of Mehurici is about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: My first question is as follows: This document has already been shown to a witness from the 306th Brigade. He testified on the 26th of October. It was shown by Ms. Benjamin. And if I told you that after an exchange of letters between the 307th [as interpreted] and the 3rd Corps, it was established that this information wasn't correct, that members of the 7th Brigade weren't in the village of Kljaci, you would agree with me, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: It would be most correct to say that I wasn't familiar with this. And a minute ago, when answering questions about this document, I said that the 7th Brigade wasn't in that area, but that perhaps there were members of the 7th who lived in that area, who had homes in that area. So it would be best and most appropriate for me to say that I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But there's a mistake on page 65, line 4. It says the 307th Brigade, and it should say the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no other questions. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have some questions I would like to put to you that are directly related to what you told both parties a while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You provided two main reasons for the presence of people in the Mehurici school. You said that on one hand, it was because there were Muslims in a certain area who had been taken by the HVO, and you said that you wanted to have an exchange. The second reason was that these people were provided with accommodation by the military authorities. As far as the first reason is concerned, if I have understood what you have said correctly, and this is why I'm asking you to clarify your answer, in your mind, there were civilians who were "detained" by the military authorities, and these Croatian civilians who were detained were going to be exchanged for Muslim civilians detained by the HVO. Have I understood the first reason correctly?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite right. As I said, the first reason was that HVO units had initiated an armed conflict. They carried out an attack on Velika Bukovica and when they did so, they took away 87 civilians. And these people were needed for an exchange. I wouldn't agree that the military authorities were involved in this and that they took care of these civilians in the course of the conflict. They were taken to the Mehurici school, but in my opinion, the civilian authorities took care of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you are telling us that the civilian authorities were in charge of them, but you said that the military authorities were also present because you personally conducted interrogations of these people.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, in a certain sense, yes, but I think I have already explained this. The military authorities were only responsible for those who were assumed to be fit for military action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, the people in the Mehurici school were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't there. I had already left, assumed other duties. After I had left, perhaps 10 days later or perhaps a little more, we assumed that the exchange would take place quite rapidly. But I think that that they stayed on for unknown reasons, perhaps for ten days or more. I couldn't be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, was there a bipartite organisation, an ABiH/HVO organisation that proceeded to carry out the exchange? Who was the superior authority that decided to exchange the inhabitants of one village for the inhabitants of another village? Do you have any information about this?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was such a body involved in the exchange. As far as the BH Army's concerned, I know this for sure, and I assume there was such an organ on the HVO side as well. And I think that the people who were responsible for this actually carried the task out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I'm following you, the army was responsible for exchanging these civilians through the intermediary of this body.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, civilians were exchanged. I think it was in the place called Dolac near Travnik. And as for those who were believed to be able-bodied men, they were taken to Zenica, and I don't know what subsequently happened to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And another question concerning another subject: You said that as a member of the 3rd Corps of the 306th Brigade security organ, you forwarded reports to the military prosecutor who was in Travnik when there were incidents reported by the military police. And with regard to this subject, with regard to this matter, the Prosecution showed you a document, Document Number 2, and I would like you to be shown this document. This document is number 1448. It's a Defence document. It's a report to the Travnik military prosecutor, a criminal report. As far as I can see -- well, can you recognise this document? Would you say that it is a report from the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This report refers to a violation committed by a number of members of the 325th Mountain Brigade. Their names are on page 1. Is that correct? Could you have a look at the last sentence in the report. You said that all information provided to the prosecution on these suspects, you said that -- you suggested that the prosecution should bring an indictment against them. Can you see the sentence? That's the conclusion of the report. It says that the prosecutor is requested to bring an indictment against them.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When there were such situations, each time the military authority represented by the security organ suggested that the Prosecutor bring an indictment when a crime was committed or when an offence was committed. Is that how matters proceeded?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: When we found out that army members, because we were above all a body that was responsible for our own members. But in this case, members of another brigade are concerned. They had traversed a lengthy route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Since you are a lawyer, and you can answer some questions put to you by the Judges. The perpetrator or the perpetrators weren't members of your brigade, they were members of the 325th Brigade. Did you have the competence to deal with it since the crimes had been committed in your area of responsibility? Is that why you referred the case to the Travnik prosecutor? Was it because the crimes had been committed in an area under your jurisdiction? Is this why you wanted them to be prosecuted? Because they weren't members of the 306th Brigade. Why not ask the commander of the 325th Brigade to do his work? Why were you involved in this?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Why were we responsible to file criminal reports against members of other brigades? Now, I think that is the question you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: We acted in this manner because these men were army members who were present in our area. They had been arrested at the site where they were attempting to commit a crime. We handed them over to the military prosecutor's office. And after having handed them over to the competent body, we had done our bit. If they thought there was good reason to proceed and to prosecute them, they would do so. They would act in accordance with the law. They would take the necessary measures. So this was an exception. We were responsible for our own members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you say that that was an exceptional circumstance. Why?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Well, because the 325th -- well, believe me, I don't know where its command was located. We weren't in contact. We weren't able to take them to their command. The roads were not practicable. We didn't have a car. We didn't have fuel. We had absolutely nothing. The simplest thing to do was to file a criminal report, to take them to the Travnik prosecutor's office, and then make sure that they took further action in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my last question, we'll go back to the Document P204 that we know well. Could you please show the witness the Document P204 which has been shown at least ten times now. In B/C/S. Could you please read out aloud paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: "Individual movement by armed persons must be stopped, and these persons must be disarmed and registered."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is the order issued to you. When someone was moving around and carrying weapons, it was necessary to stop such a person. Was this order valid for all army members?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but in my opinion, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have been told on a number of occasions - and in a certain sense you have confirmed this, too - we have been told that in Mehurici or nearby there were individuals called mujahedin who moved around and carried arms. On the basis of item 7, shouldn't these individuals have been arrested, disarmed, and shouldn't disciplinary measures have been taken against them in accordance with this order? Why was this never done? Could you explain this.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's very difficult to answer this question given the situation in the field. On the one hand, as I said, we had one defence line which was dozens of kilometres long. And we had another line facing the HVO of a similar length. We were facing two enemies and there was combat at the lines quite frequently. And if we had acted in accordance with item 7, this would have involved opening up a third line in the middle. We would have had two lines each side and a line in the middle. At the time, I think it would have been impossible to act in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have answered my question perfectly. I have one more question, since I see we have not much time left. This is the question I've wanted to ask for a long time. You have described, as well as other witnesses, something about HVO checkpoints. A number of witnesses said there were HVO checkpoints. You yourself said that there were three checkpoints: Ovnak, Zabilje, and Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Zabilje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zabilje. Three checkpoints. And you spontaneously mentioned an unfortunate incident. You said that you yourself and comrades of yours were stripped by HVO members in conditions that you described as shameful, and this took place at a checkpoint. My question is as follows: Given that there were checkpoints in this area, the mujahedin who circulated in various vehicles - in a Toyota as you said, but we don't want to advertise such vehicles - you said they were circulated in a white vehicle. There were about ten of them. They were armed. So given that there were checkpoints there, how could they pass through the HVO checkpoints? Could you explain why you - and you, too, were armed and controlled by the HVO - why were you controlled by the HVO but the others, the mujahedin, weren't, since they were circulating in the same area that you were circulating in? Could you clarify this for us, since this is an issue that has not been raised yet and it hasn't been clarified either. We have seen a map that a witness referred to, and it appears there were checkpoints almost everywhere. And if there were checkpoints, anyone passing through would be checked. As far as the mujahedin are concerned, the mujahedin who circulated in that area, are you aware of them being checked, too?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, you haven't understood me correctly. I said that there were three checkpoints in the Bila region. Ovnak, Zabilje, and Guca Gora. Initially, it was not possible for the buses to pass through; then those who were a little braver would pass through in cars, and then finally no one would pass through. So no members of the BH Army could pass through those checkpoints, nor could civilians pass through them. And as for the checkpoint at which we were humiliated and disarmed and maltreated as you said, that wasn't a checkpoint. That was an ad hoc incident because there were Croats in that area, and HVO troops lived in our area. So it's not as if we were just present in an area where there were no Croats. They, in fact, laid an ambush. They did what they did, and they then left. There were mujahedin who moved around that area, too, but they selected us. They could have chosen to do the same to them. I have my own opinion as to why they chose us and not them. But as that's not what you're asking me about, I won't address the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have almost answered my question. I see at line 73 you say that mujahedin circulated in the area. They could have been controlled just as you were. Should I draw the conclusion that they were not, in fact, controlled?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Not in the way we were. But they could have been. The same principle could have been applied. They could have been stopped and humiliated just as we were. I have my opinion about that, but I'd rather not share it at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. You're saying that you don't want to share this opinion, and I'm not going to put you in any awkward situation. Now, if I understood you well, there was a checkpoint, and there were HVO soldiers in uniform. You were passing in a uniform -- in a vehicle. The mujahedin also passed in a vehicle, but their vehicle was able to go through. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: When I was talking about this incident, I said that there was a car in front of us with four fighters armed to the tooth. But there must have been more than 50 around the vehicle. It was an ambush, a planned ambush. And we were only lucky not to have put up resistance. Had we have put up resistance, then I would probably not be here today because the ambush was really well prepared. This was not a checkpoint. It was an ambush, an ambush that served that moment. And they could have put up that ambush for the mujahedin, but they didn't. They didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you. I'll share my opinion with you. Because it would have ended differently. It would not have ended the way it did with us. That's my opinion. The outcome would have been different if they had stopped the mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. As far as the 7th Brigade is concerned, you said that the 7th Brigade was not in Mehurici, as far as you know, and no military unit was present there. But you've also told us that there could have been some soldiers, members of the 7th Brigade, who were residents of Mehurici or the general area thereof, and that they could have been there at the time. You yourself were very familiar with the region. Did you know any of the soldiers of the 7th Brigade who were residents of the region? Did you personally know any of them?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me correct you ever so slightly. I didn't say that there were no other military units in the area. In the area, there was a brigade of the BH Army, the 314th Brigade. And as for the rest of your question, whether I know any of the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, believe me, I don't know anybody, and I adhere to my words when I said that some of them resided in the area, some of their families resided in the area. They were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And I would like to repeat: As far as I know, the 7th Muslim Brigade was not there as a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Any re-examination arising from the questions that I've put to the witness? I'll give the floor to both parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe you would like to give the floor to the Prosecution. We would like to be the last, because this is our witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since Your Honour Judge Antonetti have mentioned a march starting at the Mehurici school, the Prosecution has a document in its possession which also has been disclosed to the Defence. And we would be prepared to show this, if Your Honours grant us leave to do so. This document could shed light on the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English transcript, I see you said that I've mentioned a march? I have not mentioned a march. What did I mention? Can you be more precise? Can you clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution understood that you were asking whether civilians were taken out of the school or being exchanged, so basically that at some point in time detainees in the school have been marched somewhere. And you asked also for a village to which the -- the witness mentioned a village to which members or detainees had been taken to. And we would have a document which can shed some light on this. Would you allow the Prosecution to show this? May I ask the Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence. The witness did say that the detainees were exchanged. If they were exchanged, they had to leave the school, and the Prosecution now says that there is a document that they would like to show the witness a document regarding the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Your Honour, in the description provided to us by my learned friend, I didn't recognise anything that you have referred to. Secondly, the witness has already said several times that he left the area after a certain period of time, and that it was only later on that he learned about the exchange which had taken place. And when the documents were shown to him bearing the 23rd of June or some other date, he said that he abandoned the area some seven days later and he only heard about the events that took place later on. So no such document can be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness did tell us that the exchange took place when he was no longer there. So any document that would follow his departure, you cannot show it to the witness because he was not there. In line with the objection put forth by the Defence, I cannot authorise you to put that question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can just put some additional information to Your Honours. Certainly from the Defence objection, I understand that the Defence has carefully studied the document. I just would like to inform you that Asim Delalic, the assistant commander for security of the 306th Brigade is specifically mentioned in this document, and the Prosecution believes that Mr. Asim Delalic, as an assistant commander of security of the 306th Brigade, was certainly one of the superiors of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to the Defence. But it has already been indicated that his superior at that time was this person. The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This witness will arrive, so you will have the opportunity to show him the documents. Any more questions on the part of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then we would have no questions, Your Honour. We will show the document -- we intend to show the document at a later point in time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence, please. Just a few minutes that we still have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusic, the Judge has asked you about the reasons why the people were brought there, and you repeated in your view one of the reasons was the future exchange. Where were you on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June as I already said, I was in my village, in my own village. So on the day when the large-scale conflict was taking part.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The persons that you interrogated, on the 8th of June when you were in your village, were they taken to the school on that day?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I can't be sure of that. But I assume that they were taken there on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were not in Maline on that day, and you don't know. Did anybody tell you what the reason was for these people being brought to the school?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I was in my village. And people were brought there before my arrival. When I turned up in the school in Mehurici, they were already there. I found them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In light of the fact that you've given us two reasons, are these the reasons that you are aware of as facts, or are these your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I said in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My next question arises from the question that the Judge put to you with regard to our document number 2. This is the criminal report that you filed with the district military prosecutor in Travnik. Earlier on, you said that the last time you met with the Geneva Conventions was some 30 years ago when you were a law student. Please tell me, were you engaged in criminal law at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: No, I was never engaged in criminal law. During the war, I was forced to do this because it was charged with that. I ended up doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Honourable Judge read out to you the last sentence in which you suggest that the prosecutor did something. The person who filed a criminal report in your experience, or lack of experience, rather, did it have an influence on the way you drafted such an enactment, a legal enactment?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I worked to the best of my abilities. Whether I made errors and mistakes, I don't know if I made a mistake in this particular case. There was another body which was more professional, more skilful than me, and they could put it right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also talking about the fact that in this criminal report, persons against whom the report was filed are persons from the 306th Brigade. And you said that your authority was over your own troops, but this is against the 325th Brigade. Can you please look at the document and tell us whether the damage was suffered by the building that was secured by your brigade, the transmission power line.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: This facility is in Guca Gora. Guca Gora was inhabited by the Croatian population. In Guca Gora, we tried to secure the most important facilities. Amongst them was the church, the power transmission line. There was a shoe factory as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In addition to the authority to prosecute members of the army, primarily members of your brigade, did it also apply to the facilities which enjoyed special protection by the army?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that these facilities were under your protection. So you were responsible for them. I would like to know whether the prosecution of persons who attacked facilities of the army, were they also your responsibility, or were they not your responsibility? Was that -- were they your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that they were our responsibility, to protect our property.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With regard to the fact that you reported members of a different brigade, did you inform the respective brigade if that was at all possible?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I can only respond to that from the point of view of my job. I was a legal officer. I was ordered to do things, and I did them accordingly. My superior and his superior in turn were informed what I did. Whether they informed the brigade in a question about the crime committed by their members, I can't respond to that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to talk about your knowledge as to the fact whether the mujahedin could pass the HVO points or not. Did you ever learn who the mujahedin bought their arms from?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: At that time, weapons can only be obtained on black market. As far as I know, from rumours, they obtained weapons from members of the HVO or from the Serbian side. They couldn't obtain it from Muslims because Muslims didn't have any. And why? Why would they obtain it from Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The question Your Honours have asked was relating to checkpoints, not relating to the buying of weapons by the mujahedin. This is a completely new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. However, there's a little point here. I said they drove around in their vehicle, and they were armed. Maybe that is the origin of the question. The question is very indirect; however, he has answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll have another direct question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among the members of the army, were there certain rumours that it was in the interests of the HVO to support the presence of the mujahedin in the area?

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I can just share my opinion with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just asked you whether you knew it or not. If you didn't, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: HARIS JUSIC
utterances.text: I only know that -- I can only give you my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting again, but Your Honours have asked a question relating the passing of a checkpoint by a car with mujahedin. And whether, as my learned colleague has just asked, there were certain rumours within the army that it was in the interest of the HVO to support the presence of mujahedin, the Prosecution cannot recall that such a question has been asked by Your Honours. In addition to this, my learned friend is leading her own witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team, please. We have already surpassed the time that we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to thank you. For a moment, it looked as if you would have to stay the weekend. However, we were able to finish your testimony. We would like to thank you for answering all the questions put to you. I wish you a happy journey back home and success in your career. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am looking at the Defence. Unfortunately, your second witness could not have been heard today. He will have to pass the weekend in The Hague. I hope the weekend will be pleasant for him. And we will hear this witness on Monday at quarter past 2.00. At this point in time, does the Defence wish to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We understand the situation. The witness is here. He will stay until Monday. Since our witness that has been scheduled for Monday is a doctor who is going to testify about very limited circumstances, I hope that we will be able to make up for the time due to the fact that we did not have a witness that we could bring in on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You have shown the witness five documents. Do you want to tender these documents into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender documents number 1444, 1448, 1455, and 1456, and 1266 because four of these documents were drafted by the witness himself, and he was aware of the document relative to the training of officers in the army units and in his brigade as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have shown the witness also a new document. And the witness has read from it. It was relating his position, and we would like to tender this document into evidence. And in addition, we don't have any objections to the Defence tendering their documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any objections to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you please give us five numbers for the Defence and one for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents will be admitted as DH1444, and the English version will be DH1444/E. DH1448; and the English version, 1448/E. DH1455; English version, DH1455/E. DH1456; the English version DH1456/E. And finally, DH1266; and the English version DH1266/E. As far as the Prosecution document is concerned, the Registrar notes that only one part of the document has been translated into English, and it is admitted as B/C/S version P935, and the partial translation into English will be P935/E. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that during the testimony of this witness, a name was mentioned. I believe that we should have been in private session. Maybe the witness wants to be protected. We don't know. If there are no other issues to raise, I would like to adjourn, and I invite all of you to come back on Monday at quarter past 2.00. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of November, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.53 p.m.,
